gemini.rationale: The entire company (products, operations, entity) was acquired via a reverse triangular merger, meaning T4 and T5 transferred together (gap_45 = 0). While T6 was handled selectively (subset), there is no documented structural mismatch or gap_56 indicating operations transferred without the necessary people to run them; rather, specific retention agreements were put in place.

grok.rationale: gap_45=0 because the slice states the whole company (product/asset base, corporate entity, and outstanding equity) was acquired via reverse triangular merger with no carve-out or partial-business exclusion, so Cavium’s semiconductor-processor products and the operations that produce them crossed together. gap_56=0 because the same whole-entity structure left processes inside the surviving Cavium corporation as an indirect wholly owned Marvell subsidiary; selective executive retention bonuses, two contingent offer letters, and three board designees document partial T6 continuity arrangements, not a structural detachment of processes from organization at closing. No TSA or shared-substrate operating agreement was located.

openai.rationale: The filing states that the whole company and its semiconductor product/asset base transferred with no identified carve-out, supporting coherent transfer of the customer-facing products and their associated operations and therefore gap_45=0. By contrast, management continuity was selective: only two named executive officers had post-closing offer letters, executive retention bonuses were conditional, and three Cavium designees joined Marvell’s board rather than Cavium’s management layer transferring wholesale. This documented process-versus-organization mismatch supports gap_56=1, and no cited transitional-services or operating agreement contractually absorbed that mismatch at closing.
